content.text: Momentum is a measure of how difficult it is to stop a moving object. A fast-moving car has more momentum than a slow one; a heavy truck has more momentum than a light car at the same speed. The concept of momentum is essential for understanding collisions and explosions.

Momentum (p = mv) is a vector quantity that combines mass and velocity. The law of conservation of momentum states that total momentum is always conserved in a closed system, regardless of whether the collision is elastic or inelastic.

Students often confuse momentum with kinetic energy. Momentum is always conserved in collisions, but kinetic energy is only conserved in perfectly elastic collisions. In inelastic collisions, kinetic energy is converted to other forms (heat, sound, deformation).
